---
title: "High School to College Cross-Country Performance"
format: html
---

## Research question

How are runners' high-school 5K times related to their college cross-country
times, and how might weather and course terrain help explain differences?

## Data collection

I will collect up to 2,000 U.S. college cross-country runners (men and women)
with results in the five most recent completed seasons, 2021–2025. For each
runner, I will record their best verified high-school 5K and a college 6K or 8K
result. Because these are different distances, I will keep the distance with
each time rather than compare the raw times as if they were equivalent.

TFRRS will be used to find college results. I will verify each high-school 5K
and record its source link; I will not assume a missing high-school result is
zero. I will also record the meet, date, weather, and course terrain for both
selected races where that information is available. Missing weather or terrain
information will be left blank rather than guessed.

## Data fields

Each row will represent one runner. The planned columns are:

| Field | What to record |
|---|---|
| athlete, gender, college | Runner identity and college team |
| high_school_5k, hs_race_date | Verified high-school 5K time and date |
| college_distance, college_time, college_race_date | College 6K or 8K result |
| hs_weather, college_weather | Reported conditions or temperature |
| hs_terrain, college_terrain | Course description, such as flat or hilly |
| hs_source, college_source | Links to the supporting result pages |

Weather and terrain may not be listed on TFRRS result pages, so I will only
include those variables when I can verify them from a meet or course source.

## Comparing finish times

The graphs below compare the average high-school 5K time with an estimated
college 5K time for men and women. Since the recorded college races are 6K or
8K, their times are scaled to 5K using the same average pace. These college
5K times are estimates, not actual 5K results.

To make the graphs, save the verified data as `runners.csv` in this folder.
Use one row per runner, and enter `high_school_5k` and `college_time` in
seconds (for example, 17:30 is 1,050 seconds). The CSV must also include
`gender` and `college_distance` columns.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)

if (file.exists("runners.csv")) {
  runners <- read_csv("runners.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

  required_columns <- c(
    "gender", "high_school_5k", "college_distance", "college_time"
  )

  if (!all(required_columns %in% names(runners))) {
    stop("runners.csv must include: ", paste(required_columns, collapse = ", "))
  }

  plot_data <- runners |>
    mutate(
      gender = case_when(
        tolower(gender) %in% c("female", "women", "f") ~ "Female",
        tolower(gender) %in% c("male", "men", "m") ~ "Male",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      college_distance = paste0(
        gsub("[^0-9]", "", college_distance),
        "K"
      ),
      college_distance_km = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", college_distance))
    ) |>
    filter(
      gender %in% c("Female", "Male"),
      college_distance %in% c("6K", "8K"),
      !is.na(high_school_5k),
      !is.na(college_time),
      high_school_5k > 0,
      college_time > 0
    ) |>
    mutate(college_5k_equivalent = college_time * 5 / college_distance_km)
} else {
  plot_data <- tibble(
    gender = character(),
    high_school_5k = numeric(),
    college_5k_equivalent = numeric()
  )
}

average_times <- plot_data |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  summarise(
    high_school_5k = mean(high_school_5k) / 60,
    college_5k = mean(college_5k_equivalent) / 60,
    runners = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(high_school_5k, college_5k),
    names_to = "stage",
    values_to = "average_minutes"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    stage = factor(
      recode(
        stage,
        high_school_5k = "High school",
        college_5k = "College (estimated)"
      ),
      levels = c("High school", "College (estimated)")
    )
  )
```

### Female runners

```{r}
if (nrow(average_times |> filter(gender == "Female")) > 0) {
  print(
    average_times |>
      filter(gender == "Female") |>
      ggplot(aes(x = stage, y = average_minutes)) +
      geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
      labs(
        title = "Average 5K Times: Women",
        x = NULL,
        y = "Average time (minutes)",
        caption = "College 5K times are estimated by scaling each 6K/8K result to 5K at the same pace."
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  )
} else {
  cat("Add matched female runner records to runners.csv to create this graph.")
}
```

### Male runners

```{r}
if (nrow(average_times |> filter(gender == "Male")) > 0) {

      labs(
        title = "Average 5K Times: Men",
        x = NULL,
        y = "Average time (minutes)",
        caption = "College 5K times are estimated by scaling each 6K/8K result to 5K at the same pace."

} else {
```
